skill.name: casely
skill.description: QA assistant for converting requirement documents and example cases into structured, style-consistent test cases and Excel exports.
skill.summary: Generate style-consistent QA test cases from requirements and export them for TMS import.
skill.author: JohnWayneeee

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown inline code, slash command names, paths, or code fences rather than Ruby backtick execution. A small subset is confirmed because the skill instructs dependency installation and execution of bundled Python scripts. No prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Dependency installation is initiated from skill instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin docling and openpyxl versions, document their sources, and require explicit user confirmation before running uv init, uv add, or uv sync.

remediation.issue: The workflow executes bundled local Python scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before script execution and clearly state expected reads, writes, and output directories for parser and export scripts.

remediation.issue: Project auto-detection can choose the most recently modified project.
remediation.suggestion: Ask the user to confirm the target project before parsing or exporting when more than one project directory exists.

content.user_title: Generate QA Test Cases from Requirements
content.value_statement: QA teams spend significant time turning scattered requirement documents into consistent test cases. Casely parses documents, learns team style, and exports ready-to-import Excel files.
actual_capabilities: Creates a project workspace with input, processed, results, and exports folders.
Converts PDF, DOCX, XLSX, HTML, text, and image inputs into Markdown through Docling.
Analyzes example test cases and writes a reusable test style guide.
Builds a test plan with modules, coverage tiers, risk levels, and traceability notes.
Generates atomic Markdown test cases that follow the style guide columns and tone.
Exports Markdown test case tables into individual XLSX files for TMS import.
limitations: Requires local Python dependencies, including Docling and openpyxl.
Works best when requirements and example test cases are organized in the expected project folders.
Generated test cases still need QA review before production use.
Excel export expects generated Markdown tables with clear headers and data rows.

use_cases.title: Turn Requirements into Test Suites
use_cases.description: Generate structured functional, negative, integration, or boundary cases from parsed requirement documents.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Test Writing
use_cases.description: Extract column order, wording, and formatting from existing examples before creating new cases.

use_cases.title: Prepare TMS Import Files
use_cases.description: Convert generated Markdown test cases into formatted Excel workbooks for import workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Start a QA Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new feature or product area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Initialize a Casely project named Payments and prepare folders for requirements, examples, results, and exports.

prompt_templates.title: Parse Source Documents
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert uploaded requirements and example cases into Markdown.
prompt_templates.prompt: Parse the Payments project documents and report which requirement and example files were converted successfully.

prompt_templates.title: Create Style and Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a reusable style guide and coverage plan before generation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the parsed examples, create the style guide, then plan functional, negative, and boundary coverage for each module.

prompt_templates.title: Generate and Export Cases
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for producing import-ready deliverables.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the approved style guide and test plan, generate functional and negative cases for checkout, then export them to Excel.

output_examples.input: A QA engineer initializes a Payments project for new requirement documents and existing example cases.
output_examples.output: Casely creates the project folder structure, checks the expected dependencies, and tells the user where to place source files.

output_examples.input: A QA lead asks Casely to learn from parsed example test cases.
output_examples.output: Casely produces a style guide with the detected columns, writing style, language, and formatting rules for future cases.

output_examples.input: A release manager asks for TMS-ready exports after cases are generated.
output_examples.output: Casely converts each generated Markdown test case into a matching Excel file in the exports folder.

best_practices: Review and approve the generated style guide before creating test cases.
Keep requirement files and example cases in separate input folders.
Confirm the target project before parsing or exporting when multiple projects exist.
anti_patterns: Generating cases before examples have been parsed and reviewed.
Changing expected columns without updating the style guide first.
Importing generated cases into a TMS without QA validation.

faq.question: What document types can Casely process?
faq.answer: It can process common document, spreadsheet, text, web, and image formats supported by Docling.

faq.question: Does Casely replace QA review?
faq.answer: No. It accelerates drafting, but QA owners should verify coverage, accuracy, and business rules.

faq.question: Can it match our existing test case format?
faq.answer: Yes. It analyzes example cases and uses the resulting style guide as the generation template.

faq.question: Can it generate different test types?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow supports functional, negative, integration, boundary, security, and other named case types.

faq.question: What does the Excel export produce?
faq.answer: It creates individual XLSX files from generated Markdown tables, using the detected headers as spreadsheet columns.

faq.question: Does it need local setup?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow expects local Python tooling and the Docling and openpyxl dependencies.
